# War Scroll Column 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 1QM (Cave 1), Col. 6 | **Condition:** complete

---

**1** The men of the shield line shall be arranged, one thousand on each side, and the shields shall cover the front of the rank so that none is exposed to the weapons of the enemy.

**2** The infantry shall be arranged rank upon rank. The men of the first rank shall hold spears of bronze, seven cubits in length, with points of polished iron.

**3** The men of the second rank shall hold shields and javelins, and they shall stand prepared behind the first battle line to strengthen the formation.

**4** The trumpeters shall station themselves behind the battle line — six priests blowing upon the trumpets of assembly — and they shall hold the trumpets of signal in their hands continually.

**5** They shall blow upon them a sustained blast for the advance of battle, and the infantry shall go forth to the battle lines of the enemy.

**6** Then they shall blow upon the trumpets of retreat, a broken blast, to signal the return of the men to the first rank when they have completed their engagement.

**7** In seven lots of engagement shall the Sons of Light prevail in three, subduing wickedness; and the Sons of Darkness shall prevail in three, bringing low the army of light.

**8** But in the seventh lot, the great hand of God shall subdue Belial and all the angels of his dominion and all the men of his lot.

**9** The holy ones shall shine forth to the aid of truth, to the destruction of the Sons of Darkness. There shall be great slaughter before the God of Israel,

**10** for this is the day appointed by Him from of old for the war of annihilation against the Sons of Darkness. On that day the congregation of the divine ones and the assembly of men shall engage in great slaughter.

**11** They shall blow upon the trumpets of signal for the ordering of the battle ranks into their divisions against all the battle lines of the enemy.

**12** Upon the trumpets of assembly they shall blow a sustained blast for the deployment of battle, and the priests shall blow upon the six trumpets of the slain a shrill staccato blast.

**13** Upon the trumpets of ambush they shall blow a signal for the opening of the gates of war, and the infantry shall go forth and take their stations in their ranks.

**14** The horsemen shall be stationed to the right and to the left of the battle formation, and their cavalry shall be deployed on both flanks, spreading outward to cause fear.

**15** There shall be one thousand horsemen alongside the men of the battle line: five hundred on the right flank and five hundred on the left.

**16** Their horses shall be swift stallions, soft of mouth, long of wind, full in their measure, mature but not aged, trained for battle and accustomed to the sounds of war.

**17** Those who ride upon them shall be men of valor, skilled in horsemanship, ranging in age from thirty years to forty-five years.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 6 is well preserved. The seven-lot battle structure (lines 7-10) articulates the scroll's eschatological conviction that divine intervention in the seventh engagement is decisive. "Lots" (goralot) denotes divinely apportioned rounds of battle. Trumpet terminology follows the scroll's distinctive liturgical-military vocabulary.*
